summary: Verified the Admin.tsx rules-of-hooks fix. All useState/useEffect hooks (incl. the moved `dz` state at line 54, and later `creators`/`creatorSearch`/`creatorResults`/`support`/`supportThread`/`supportReplyText` at lines 96-101, plus dmAccess at 69, reqHandle at 70) are declared BEFORE the early `return <Navigate to="/" replace />` at line 136. No hooks are called after the early return. Verified in both /app/src/pages/Admin.tsx and the synced /app/frontend/src/pages/Admin.tsx (files are identical). ESLint reports no react-hooks/rules-of-hooks violations. Playwright UI tests passed for all 4 requested scenarios.

issues: Danger zone (Promote / Purge demo) is rendered for moderators too, not just full admins. The page itself does render for moderators (`can_moderate` allows it), but production-bootstrap tools arguably should be gated behind `isFull` or `isSuper`. Not part of this review's scope — flagging for awareness.

critical_code_review_comments: Admin.tsx is 766 lines — exceeds recommended 700-line threshold; main agent may want to extract DangerZone, DmAccessPanel, RolesPanel, UsersList, SupportModal, DmReviewModal into separate components in a future refactor.

Several useState declarations are still scattered (lines 69-70 dmAccess/reqHandle, 96-101 creators/support cluster) rather than grouped at the top; this works but is fragile — any future edit that places a new useState below line 136 would re-introduce the exact bug just fixed. Consider grouping all hooks in a `// --- state ---` block right after `useAuth()` and adding an ESLint rule to lint this directory on CI.

rca of the issue: Original bug (now fixed): `const [dz, setDz] = useState(false)` was declared AFTER the early `return <Navigate to="/" replace />`. When a staff member's role was revoked mid-session while they were on /admin, the component would re-render, hit the early-return path, and React would see fewer hooks than the previous render → 'Rendered fewer hooks than expected' crash. Fix: moved `useState` call to line 54, before line 136's early return. Verified by demotion-and-reload regression test — no hook mismatch error observed.
